title: Lockstep scalability on AWS c7i.48xlarge (B2, B2-F45): (a) RTF vs links (log-log) for every element count N, static (F1) and with mobility (F3), with the RTF = 1 line and the isolation reference points run alone; (b) RTF vs links for the feature sets F0-F4 at N = 240; (c) aggregate RX throughput vs links for four sample rates; (d) one-link RTF vs the number of surfaces; (e) RTF vs numba threads; (f) F5 (native ZMQ data plane, end to end) vs F4 of the same rerun
sremu_dirty_note: not determined: figure scripts start no git process; a final build checks clean trees before it runs any script
assumptions: SIM benchmark scenes (LOS and RIS paths, one carrier at 3.5 GHz, non-zero RIS path asserted per scene); the workload is not a physics result
11 points ran concurrently (16 vCPUs each); isolation reference points rerun alone were 0.99-1.16x faster (open markers)
aggregate throughput = n_rx * f_s * RTF (one rate group per scene)
(a)-(e): B2 run at 309c633; (f): B2-F45 rerun at bf08268 on another instance of the same type, F5 end-to-end RTF against F4 of the same run (not compared with (a)-(e))
(e): thread counts above 16 ran in tier-4 slots of as many vCPUs, the others in 16-vCPU slots; all points packed
points below the pilot floor (9 heavy F3 points) and failed points are not drawn
